title: The Lights of Geoncheonggung
synopsis: The first electric lamps of Korea go dark for an hour.
In the dark, two strangers walk through the Queen's court.
goal: Find out what the strangers were doing in the dark, and why the Queen is in danger.

options.feedback: The note says he did not touch the fire. Read it again.

options.label: The belt on the big wheel
The coal box

notes: Played as a look round (ExploreScene): Lady Han's water-drop note lies under the coal scoop; the lamp machine opens the three choice pictures once it is read.

Measured 2026-11-06 on the grid sheet of lamp_house.webp (picture.measuredOn): the scoop and the note lower left, the window with the pavilion, the engine with its wheel and belt, the coal heap, the open door, the wires along the top; no two areas overlap.

The three choice pictures differ by what the note says (the fire, the coal, the leather belt on the big wheel), never by colour alone. The note is drawn as a blank paper with a small blue water-drop mark: no writing in any picture.
Puzzle kind chosen by hand: the season spread assigns Case 05 a look round with a picture choice (PART 10 brief); the note is read in the place, then the part is matched by its words.

learning.objective: 궁녀 한씨의 쪽지에서 did not touch 문장(불, 석탄)을 읽어 지우고, 낯선 이가 벗겨 낸 것(큰 바퀴의 가죽 띠)을 그림에서 고른다.
expressions: He did not touch the fire.
He took off the long leather belt.

play.title: The Lamp House
story: South of the pond stands the lamp house.
Its machine makes the light for the King's and the Queen's halls.
Last night it stopped for an hour. Who stopped it? Look for marks.
play.letterIntro: Under the coal scoop, a note in the King's letters, with a small water drop:
play.letter:
Detective,
Last night the lamps did not go out on their own.
One of the two strangers came into the lamp house.
He did not touch the fire. He did not touch the coal.
He took off the long leather belt that turns the big wheel.
I put it back at dawn. His muddy hand is still on it.
play.question: What did the stranger touch? Tap one picture.
hints: Find the note under the coal scoop first. Then look at the machine.
Two things in the note are things he did NOT touch.
play.successMessage: A muddy hand mark on the belt!
transition: The lamps often blink on and off. Everyone thought it was that again.
But this dark was made on purpose.
Lady Han knows more. You follow her to the Queen's court.

clue.title: The Dark Was Made
clue.note: The lamps did not fail. A stranger took the belt off the big wheel on purpose.

evidence.name: Lady Han's Note
evidence.description: Lady Han's note in the King's letters, marked with her water drop. The dark was made on purpose. A stranger took off the belt on the big wheel.

talk.speaker: lady_han
talk.goal: Find out why the dark matters.

lines.text: You found my note. Good. I wrote no name. The strangers may read it too.
The water drop is my mark. I carry the Queen's water each dawn.
The lamps blink every week. Nobody looks twice.
So the strangers hid in a dark that seemed normal.

discovery.title: THE DARK WAS MADE
discovery.detail: Someone took the belt off on purpose. The strangers needed the dark.

notes: Letter: Lady Han's account of the night, in before/after words, told out of order (9:00 first): following the lines from the top gives the wrong order. 8:00 and 9:00 are fixed; the guards at the main gate are not part of it (another gate, far away). The flat board foreshadows the final.
Every card is made up (fiction): the night and the strangers are the case's own.
Cards are listed hall, guards, dark, lit, gate, back, lamphouse: never in the answer's order (the board does not shuffle).

clueInputs.note: The dark was made: the belt was taken off.
Lady Han's note from the lamp house: the night begins there.

learning.objective: 한씨의 진술에서 after, only after, before 표현을 읽고, 순서가 섞인 말을 그날 밤 일어난 순서대로 놓는다.
expressions: only after the lamps went dark

play.title: One Hour in the Dark
story: Lady Han meets you in the Queen's court.
She saw where the strangers went.
"Put my words in order," she says.
play.letter:
The lamp man came back at 9:00. By then, the men were gone.
Before the Queen's hall, the men stood at the east gate.
One man had a flat board under his arm.
They went to the east gate only after the lamps went dark.
The lamps went dark after the strangers came into the lamp house.
The lamp man lit the lamps at 8:00.
The guards at the main gate saw nothing. They are far away.
play.question: Put the night in order, from 8:00 to 9:00.
hints: Find after and before in Lady Han's words. Her words are not in order.
The main gate is far away. Is it part of that night?
play.successMessage: The strangers walked straight to the Queen's hall!
transition: From the east gate to the Queen's hall, in one hour of dark.
"They whispered numbers," Lady Han says. "Ten, twenty, thirty…"
You look under the Queen's steps. A long rope with knots lies there!
play.orderFeedback: Read Lady Han's words again. What came after the dark?

lines.text: I sleep near the Queen's rooms.
Last night I heard steps in the dark.

notes: A number read in words: the knot rule (a big knot is ten steps, a small knot is one) and the knots on the rope the detective found. The strangers' board in the final counts its dots the same way.

clueInputs.note: The strangers counted between the east gate and the Queen's hall.

learning.objective: 매듭 규칙(A big knot is ten steps. A small knot is one step.)을 읽고 매듭 수를 걸음 수로 바꿔 입력한다.
expressions: A big knot is ten steps.
three big knots, then seven small knots

play.title: The Knotted Rope
story: You found the rope under the Queen's steps.
One stranger dropped it as the lamps came back.
"Builders measure with ropes like this," Lady Han says.
play.letterIntro: Lady Han looks at the knots and says:
play.letter:
Builders measure with ropes like this.
A big knot is ten steps. A small knot is one step.
The rope starts at the east gate.
It ends at the Queen's door.
On it are three big knots, then seven small knots.
play.question: How many steps is it from the east gate to the Queen's door?
hints: Read what one big knot means, and what one small knot means.
Count the big knots in tens. Then add the small knots.
play.successMessage: Thirty-seven steps, from the east gate to the Queen's door!
transition: Why measure a path? To draw a map of it.
You remember the man with the flat board. You look behind the steps again.
There it is, in the leaves: a flat board with lines and dots!
"The King must see this," Lady Han says.

feedback.10: That counts every knot as one step. A big knot is ten steps.
feedback.30: You counted the big knots. Now add the small ones.
feedback.73: The big knots are tens, not ones. Read Lady Han's rule again.

play.orderFeedback: The right numbers, in the wrong order. Big knots are the tens.

clue.title: Thirty-Seven Steps
clue.note: The rope measures 37 steps from the east gate to the Queen's door.

evidence.name: The Knotted Rope
evidence.description: A stranger's measuring rope: 37 steps from the east gate to the Queen's door.

discovery.title: THEY MEASURED THE WAY
discovery.detail: Nobody measures a path for no reason. What were they making?

notes: The strangers' board read with the rope's rule: big dot = ten steps, small dot = one. The circled door is 37 steps from the east gate (M3, e3; the walk from the east gate, M2, e2); the far door is 52 with no circle; the square with an X and a wheel by the pond is the lamp house (M1, e1), not a door. Only the Queen's hall fits.

A text choice of the three places (2026-11-09 PART 7): the three are places the detective has already been, so their pictures would show the answer's picture before the choice (season_playthrough 'nothing given away'). The board itself is told in words. Answer listed last.
The history (h4, h5) is told after the answer, plainly and once: in the transition and the ending.

clueInputs.note: The lamp house is where the dark was made: the square with the X and the wheel.
The strangers walked from the east gate to the Queen's hall.
37 steps from the east gate to the Queen's door: the circled door's dots.

learning.objective: 판의 설명(three big dots and seven small dots, a door with a circle)을 밧줄 매듭 규칙으로 읽어 37걸음 문을 찾고, 그 문이 왕비의 처소임을 그림에서 고른다.
expressions: three big dots and seven small dots

play.title: The Board with No Names
story: You bring the strangers' board to the King and the Queen.
It has no names. Only lines, dots and marks.
The Queen asks, "Whose door is marked?"
play.letter:
A line starts at the east gate.
It goes to a door with a circle.
By the circled door: three big dots and seven small dots.
Another line goes to a far door. By it: five big dots and two small dots. No circle.
By the pond is a square with an X. A wheel is drawn in the square.
The dots count like the knots on the rope.
play.question: Whose door has the circle? Tap the picture.
hints: A big dot is ten steps. A small dot is one step, like the rope.
Your rope measured 37 steps from the east gate. To whose door?
play.successMessage: The circle is the Queen's door: 37 steps from the east gate!
transition: "And the X is the lamp house," says the King. "They will make the dark again."
Lady Han says, "Japan wants more power in Korea. The Queen works with Russia to stop it."
The King folds the map slowly.

evidence.name: The Strangers' Map
evidence.description: The strangers' board, with no names. A circle marks the Queen's door, 37 steps from the east gate. An X marks the lamp house.

ending.text: Thank you, Detective. I will keep this map.
ending.speaker: gojong

ending.text: Now I know they are watching me.
ending.speaker: myeongseong

ending.text: Korea must choose its own way. I will not stop.
ending.speaker: myeongseong

ending.text: The map shows the way to the Queen's door.
In 1895, the Queen worked with Russia to stop Japan's power from growing.
On 8 October 1895, men sent by Japan's minister attacked the palace.
The Queen was killed in that attack.
I will not forget the truth of these days.

learningGoal.titleKo: 한 일과 하지 않은 일 구별해 읽기

objectives: Find out why the lamps went dark.
Count the steps on the rope.
Find whose door the map marks.
intro: Autumn, 1895. This morning, the King has called you, a detective, to Geoncheonggung.
Here, inside the great palace, the King and the Queen live.
In 1887, the first electric lamps in Korea were lit here.
They often blink on and off. People call them the good-for-nothing lights.
Last night they went dark for an hour.
And two strangers were seen in the Queen's court.
play.caseSummary: Strangers made the lamps go dark. They measured the way from the east gate to the Queen's door. Court Lady Han left a note with her water drop. The detective found the strangers' rope and their map. The map's circle marked the Queen's door. In 1895 the Queen worked with Russia to hold back Japan's power. On 8 October 1895, men sent by Japan's minister attacked the palace, and the Queen was killed.

notes: Season 5 Case 05 (PART 10, 2026-11-06). Set weeks before the Eulmi incident; the attack is told once, plainly, in the final's ending and the reveal, never shown.

The Queen is never drawn with a detailed face: no reliable photograph of her is known, and her portrait is seen from behind (manifest). She, the King and Lady Han speak made-up words (dossier fiction).
